MT_CAP_LLM.description: Local large-language-model inference via llama.cpp, plus model discovery and download.
MT_CAP_LLM.implies_note: HTTPS, not merely HTTP, and it is settled rather than assumed: CLlamaModelManager.cpp:228 builds EVERY model URL as https://huggingface.co/..., and httplib::Client on an https:// host without TLS support fails at runtime. LLM=1 HTTPS=0 would build, link and be unable to fetch any model -- the succeeds-and-lies shape #3.4 abolishes. There is no plain-HTTP model source in the tree, so splitting the downloader would buy a configuration nothing uses.
MT_CAP_LLM.app_visible_note: Corrected from false on 2026-09-06. The measurement behind the old value -- no app GUARDS on MT_ENABLE_LLAMA_CPP -- was true and is the wrong test. The right one is FFmpeg's: a flag is app-visible if it appears in a header app TUs include. GUI/Helpers/CGuiViewLlamaModelLoader.h is now guarded on MT_ENABLE_LLAMA_CPP (it owns a CLlamaModelDownloader, which owns a CFileDownloader, which needs httplib), and the template includes that header inside its own `#if MT_CAP_LLM`. With the flag engine-only the header declared nothing in an app TU while the app believed the capability was on, and the app failed to compile against an incomplete type.

MT_CAP_LLM.acquisition_note: No Linux entry: platform/Linux/build-llama-cpp.sh was named here but has never existed. On Linux llama.cpp is built IN-TREE by the engine's own CMake (add_subdirectory(other/lib/llama.cpp), CMakeLists.txt:428), not acquired into the keyed deps bucket. Found 2026-09-03 by the L16 gate test, which checks that every acquisition path resolves to a file.

MT_CAP_VIDEO_PLAYBACK.description: Video decoding and playback: FFmpeg, libvpx, opus, nestegg, and the platform hardware decoders.
MT_CAP_VIDEO_PLAYBACK.app_visible_note: MT_ENABLE_FFMPEG appears in Video/CVideoSourceFFmpeg.h:10, a header app TUs include, AND one host app guards on it 40 times in its own src/. Both routes to app-visible are exercised by this one flag. MT_ENABLE_WEBM_VPX (added 2026-08-31, unification plan Phase 2) gates the legacy nestegg/vpx/opus lane -- CVideoSourceWebMVpx compiled unconditionally before, which made MT_CAP_VIDEO_PLAYBACK=0 an engine-blocked configuration: the link died on opus_*/vpx_* against the stub archive.
MT_CAP_VIDEO_PLAYBACK.conditional_headers_note: Was eight entries; six of them stopped being conditional in fd75d490/da10184f and only their explanatory COMMENTS still name MT_ENABLE_FFMPEG. Trimmed 2026-09-10 to the two that really are gated. The six OS-native decoder headers -- AACMF, WMAMF, WMVMF, HEVCVT, HEVCMF, MFComThreadGuard -- are now platform-only on purpose: each survives precisely when FFmpeg does not, which is what makes an OS-decode store build possible. Listing them here claimed the opposite.

dependencies.name: FFmpeg
dependencies.provenance: downloaded tarball
dependencies.note: THE FLAG AND THE FALSE ARE BOTH LOAD-BEARING, and neither was here before 2026-09-10. Without `flag` this row was emitted into LICENSES.txt even at MT_ENABLE_FFMPEG=0, so a store build shipping no FFmpeg still declared one -- a false statement to users, made by the build (tracker 3.9). commercial_safe was `true`, which flatly contradicted the store rule this programme exists to satisfy (tracker 3.4): LGPL-2.1 #6 cannot be discharged inside a signed, receipt-checked, library-validated store bundle, and shipping it as a dylib does NOT discharge it. With both fields present the deny-list means what it says -- MT_COMMERCIAL_BUILD=1 with MT_ENABLE_FFMPEG=1 now REFUSES TO RESOLVE, and a commercial build must set MT_ENABLE_FFMPEG=0. It fires for none of the four apps' shipped manifests, which all resolve MT_COMMERCIAL_BUILD=0. The version is the real one now rather than 'see platform/*/build-video_codecs.*', which meant the library a user may exercise their #6(b) right to replace could not be identified from the document granting it (tracker 3.2).

commercial.note: NOT a whole-capability veto. Video playback stays fully on and a decoder SET is withheld. A boolean field would describe none of this correctly.

ffmpeg.note: The FFmpeg decoder policy, in one place. Three build scripts used to carry their own copies of these lists -- and of the guard sets derived from them -- so a name added in one platform's script was invisible to the other two and to the licence scanner. What is NOT here, deliberately: FFmpeg's implicit selects (h263 arrives with mpeg4, its parser with mpeg4video) and the object-file names, which are facts about a pinned FFmpeg version rather than policy, and belong beside that pin in the scripts.
ffmpeg.decoders_withheld_note: Patent-encumbered, and withheld from every DISTRIBUTED build -- the public/free tier as much as the store tier, because patents attach to distribution rather than to payment. Present only when the resolved mode is `full`, which mtcaps gives only to MT_PRIVATE_BUILD=1. This list was commercial.forbidden_decoders_commercial until 2026-09-02; the licence scanners read it here now.
ffmpeg.parsers_note: A parser is not a decoder: hevc and aac parse in both modes because parsing a bitstream infringes nothing. Only the vc1 parser follows its decoder into full mode.
ffmpeg.demuxers_note: Identical in both modes -- asf demuxing is licensing-safe under Microsoft's Open Specification Promise -- and none select-depends on another demuxer.

symbols.symbols_note: The leading alternative is [^A-Za-z0-9]av_ and NOT a bare av_, which was a false positive with teeth: the patterns are grep -E against whole nm lines, so `av_` matched miniaudio's ma_dr_wav_alaw_to_f32 and every other ma_dr_wav_* symbol, and MT_CAP_VIDEO_PLAYBACK=0 failed the capability matrix from the day miniaudio landed -- for a library that has nothing to do with video. A symbol-start class fixes it without narrowing what is actually forbidden: nm writes _av_free on macOS and av_free elsewhere, and both are preceded by a non-alphanumeric.

MT_CAP_HTTP.description: Plain HTTP client (cpp-httplib) and the shared file downloader.
MT_CAP_HTTP.app_visible_note: Corrected from false on 2026-09-06. THREE of the four apps include httplib.h directly -- the template's file-downloader example, one host's REST client, and a game's lobby, asset-sync and eight test files -- so an engine-only flag was simply wrong. It mattered the moment the capability got real guards: engine_only_defines() keeps such a flag out of MT_CAPS_DEFINES, the app xcconfigs read only that, and the Windows ide-defines-app.txt omits it, so an app-side `#if MT_ENABLE_HTTPLIB` evaluated to 0 on macOS and Windows however the capability resolved -- while Linux mt_apply_capabilities marks every define PUBLIC and got it right. A guard that disagrees across platforms is worse than no guard.
MT_CAP_HTTP.ownership_note: MT_CAP_HTTP OWNS cpp-httplib. MT_CAP_LLM depends on it and must not own it: Tools/NetGame/CFileDownloader.cpp is a shared consumer independent of any LLM, so leaving httplib inside the llama.cpp submodule makes a plain HTTP-only app pay for a 598 MB dependency to download a file. #5.3 done 2026-09-09: cpp-httplib is vendored under other/lib/cpp-httplib, copied verbatim from the llama.cpp vendor tree and independent of the llama.cpp submodule; the two engine wrapper includes (src/Engine/Libs/httplib/httplib.h and httplib_vendor.cpp) point there.

symbols.symbols_note: Was empty in both directions -- the capability was declared and guarded nothing, so nothing could be asserted about it either. ma_decoder_ is the honest marker: miniaudio is compiled decode-only and its decoder entry points are what a music-player build links that a non-music build must not. CSlrMusicFile* are the engine's own classes and appear only when the player is compiled in. CSlrMusicFileResampled WAS listed here and is not any more; the removal is a CORRECTION, not a relaxation. Since the 2026-09-10 resampling refactor it is CSlrMusicFileOgg's base class, and Ogg is CORE -- it is present at MT_CAP_MUSIC_PLAYER=0 today (46 symbols, measured) and always was. A pattern that forbids a core class's base forbids the core class, so it failed the matrix the moment the refactor landed and said nothing true when it passed.

MT_CAP_TEST_ENGINE.app_visible_note: Appears in three headers app TUs include, and all four apps' src/Tests/ guard on it. Renamed from ENABLE_IMGUI_TEST_ENGINE in Phase 1 -- do not emit both spellings. GUARD WITH #if, NEVER #ifdef: this flag is emitted as =0 rather than absent, and #ifdef is true for a macro defined as 0, so an #ifdef guard compiles app code in while the engine has compiled its half out. DummyApp (6 sites) and c64d (9) both had that defect until 2026-08-28. The eight vendored src/Engine/Libs/imgui_test_engine/*.cpp are guarded the same way and registered in that directory's MTENGINE_PATCHES.md -- without those guards MT_CAP_TEST_ENGINE=0 does not build at all, because imconfig.h has already removed the hooks they need.

MT_CAP_OPENCV.description: OpenCV 5 core, imgproc, geometry and features, built from the pinned source tarball. Images cross the engine boundary through src/Engine/OpenCV/MT_OpenCV.h.
MT_CAP_OPENCV.implies_note: Nothing, deliberately. The bridge reads and writes CImageData and never asks a codec to open a file, so an app that wants OpenCV to see a JPEG turns MT_CAP_PHOTO_CODECS on as well -- rather than an implication hiding a 40 MB codec bundle behind a vision capability.
MT_CAP_OPENCV.app_visible_note: Apps include OpenCV headers directly and gate their own views on MT_CAP_OPENCV; the engine supplies only the CImageData <-> cv::Mat bridge.
MT_CAP_OPENCV.note: THE FIRST CAPABILITY WHOSE DEFAULT IS 0. Every other capability defaults to 1 and its acquisition script spells the fallback ${MT_ENABLE_X:-1}, so a bare engine clone builds everything. OpenCV must not: turning it on downloads 154 MB of tarballs and builds a second computer-vision library, and only two of the five apps want it. Its script therefore spells the fallback :-0, the standalone xcconfig and CMake defaults say 0, and absent means OFF.
MT_CAP_OPENCV.naming_note: It keeps the library name. There is no engine feature to abstract -- the engine's own OpenCV surface is one bridge header, and every host that turns this on calls the cv:: API directly -- so the library name IS the capability.

Its patent expired in 2020, it moved into the main repository in 4.4, and in 5.0 it lives in the features module -- so MT_CAP_OPENCV alone gives SIFT, ORB, BRISK, FAST, MSER and SimpleBlobDetector. What this capability adds is SURF, still patented and still compiled only under OPENCV_ENABLE_NONFREE, together with the descriptors that moved to contrib in 5.0.
MT_CAP_OPENCV_NONFREE.ownership_note: One build unit and one archive serve both capabilities: it is a single CMake configure, so the per-unit store is keyed by both keys and a flip here rebuilds rather than reusing a tree configured without contrib.

MT_CAP_YOLO.description: Object detection: OpenCV 5's dnn module, an ONNX model catalogue and a downloader. Ships no model weights.
MT_CAP_YOLO.implies_note: OPENCV because the detector IS OpenCV's dnn module. HTTPS as well as HTTP because every catalogue URL is https://huggingface.co/..., and httplib::Client on an https host without TLS support fails at runtime -- the same pairing, for the same reason, that MT_CAP_LLM carries.
MT_CAP_YOLO.app_visible_note: The template guards its own model-selector and camera-demo views on MT_CAP_YOLO, and includes engine headers that are guarded on MT_ENABLE_YOLO.
MT_CAP_YOLO.note: IT OWNS NO SCRIPT OF ITS OWN, but it does own the ARCHIVE'S CONTENT. build-opencv.* already produces libmt_opencv.a; this capability makes that one configure add `dnn` and bundled protobuf to it -- 45 MB with, 16.6 MB without, measured. So it names the same acquisition scripts and artefacts as MT_CAP_OPENCV and keys the deps bucket alongside it: resolve.deps_key_capabilities says a key that carries less REUSES A WRONG ARCHIVE, and two different archives at one path is exactly what an empty acquisition table would have produced.
MT_CAP_YOLO.ownership_note: It also joins the opencv build unit's `reads`, so the per-unit store is keyed by all three OpenCV-family capabilities. One CMake configure serves them all.
